The constraint we start with

What slows fitness & wellness teams down.

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

01

Inquiries go cold before anyone replies

People message after an Instagram reel, an ad or a Google search, often late in the evening. When the reply waits for the next shift, they book a trial, appointment or discovery call somewhere else, and the ad spend that brought them is wasted.

02

Members drift away quietly

Most members do not cancel; they come less, then stop. By the renewal date the habit is gone. Access logs and bookings show the drift weeks earlier, but trainers and front desks rarely see who has slipped until it is too late to help.

03

No-shows and gaps waste capacity you cannot resell

An empty spin bike, a missed facial slot or an unfilled retreat place cannot be sold again. Waitlists live on paper or in personal chats, and late cancellations, deposits and no-show fees are handled differently by every staff member.

04

Renewals, freezes and payments run on memory

Renewal reminders, freeze requests, part payments and failed auto-debits are tracked in registers and personal WhatsApp. Policies are applied inconsistently, and members feel surprised by a debit or trapped when they cannot find how to cancel.

05

Body and health data needs care, and advice must stay in its lane

Measurements, progress photos, health declarations and food logs need consent and tight access. Trainers and coaches must not drift into medical advice, and marketing must avoid unsupported weight-loss, inch-loss or beauty claims.

06

Commissions and incentives are disputed every month

Stylists, therapists and trainers are paid on services, packages and retail sold. When the numbers come from spreadsheets and memory, staff cannot see where they stand and month end turns into a negotiation.

The perfect automation

Attendance-to-renewal retention loop

One connected loop from the first weeks of a membership to the renewal decision. Check-ins, bookings and plan dates flow into one member record. Members who drift below their own usual pattern reach their trainer or teacher with context and a drafted personal note, consented nudges help them back, and renewals, freezes and failed payments follow one written policy with every decision recorded.

  1. 01

    Bring visits, bookings and plans together

    Access control check-ins, class bookings, PT balances, plan end dates and payment status sync nightly into one member record, through each system's API or scheduled exports. We read check-in events only; biometric templates stay in the access system.

    nn8nSSupabase
  2. 02

    Compare each member with their own pattern

    Readable rules flag a regular who has missed twice their usual gap, a class-pack holder whose credits are about to expire, or a PT client with no session booked. New joiners, approved freezes and travel are excluded, so trainers see real drift rather than noise.

    PPythonSSupabase
  3. 03

    Brief the trainer with a drafted note

    Each morning, trainers and teachers see their flagged members with usual training time, last class, renewal date and the latest note, plus a short personal message drafted by AI for them to edit. Nothing is sent until the trainer approves it.

    RRetoolACAnthropic Claude
  4. 04

    Nudge back with consent, route health to people

    Members who opted in get an approved WhatsApp template in their trainer's name, such as a class that fits their schedule. When they reply, the trainer's own note follows inside the 24-hour window. Replies that mention injury, illness or pregnancy go to a person, who suggests checking with a doctor.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8n
  5. 05

    Renew, freeze or cancel on clear terms

    Ahead of the end or renewal date, members get the price, date and options to renew, change, freeze or cancel. Payments run through gateway links, UPI Autopay or card mandates, freezes follow the written policy, and failed debits get a polite notice with a fresh link.

    WBWhatsApp Business Platformnn8n
  6. 06

    One retention view for the owner

    A dashboard shows flagged members worked, members who returned, renewals, freezes, cancellations and recovered payments by location, trainer and plan, so the owner can see which follow-ups bring people back.

    MPMicrosoft Power BISSupabase

Human checkpoint

Trainers and teachers decide whether to reach out and approve every message. The manager approves freezes outside policy, refunds, transfers and any discount. Health-related replies are handled by a person and referred to a doctor where needed. Cancellations are always honored and access is never blocked automatically.

What changes

  • Trainers hear about members who are drifting while there is still time to help, not after the plan has lapsed
  • Renewals, freezes, cancellations and failed payments handled the same way every time, with a clear record
  • Members get personal, relevant check-ins from people they know instead of generic offers
  • Owners see retention by location, trainer and plan in one place

Automation playbook

Start where the work repeats.

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Discover, inquire and try · 2–3 weeks

Coaching inquiry and discovery call funnel

Turn Instagram comments and DMs, ad leads and WhatsApp messages into booked discovery calls with a short pre-call form, so coaches speak to prepared prospects and nobody waits days for a reply.

View the blueprint ↗Discover, inquire and try · 3–5 weeks

Trial class booking and membership conversion

Book trial classes and intro offers straight from ads, Google and WhatsApp, prepare the trainer or teacher, and follow up after the visit with published plans and a payment link, so every trial visitor gets a consistent path to membership.

View the blueprint ↗Join, pay and onboard · 4–6 weeks

Coaching intake and qualified plan workflow

Collect consented intake details through a secure form, route them to a qualified dietitian or nutritionist, and let AI handle the formatting work around the plan the professional writes, such as shopping lists and recipe swaps.

View the blueprint ↗Join, pay and onboard · 3–5 weeks

Retreat, workshop and teacher training enrollment

Run applications, deposits, installments, health declarations, room allocation and pre-arrival information for retreats, workshops and teacher trainings from one record, with the lead teacher deciding every application that needs judgment.

View the blueprint ↗Book, attend and visit · 3–4 weeks

Class booking, waitlists and automatic promotion

Let members book classes on WhatsApp or the app, hold fair waitlists, offer the next person a spot when one opens, and apply the late cancellation policy the same way every time.

Salon booking, reminders and no-show handling

Book the right service with the right stylist or therapist for the right length of time, send reminders and patch test prompts, fill late gaps from a waitlist, and handle no-shows with one clear policy.

How we work

A clear delivery rhythm, from discovery to daily operation.

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 01 · 1–2 weeksDiscover

    We spend time at the front desk, on the gym floor, at the salon reception or with the coaching team to see how inquiries, bookings, renewals and check-ins really happen, and which systems hold the data. We confirm what the gym, salon or coaching software allows through APIs or exports, and choose the first journey to automate.

  2. 02 · 1–2 weeksDesign

    We design booking, reminder, follow-up and renewal flows, intake and check-in forms, routing rules and approval points, and write templates for WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email. Consent wording, health declarations, photo handling and retention are designed with the client's compliance owner, and a head trainer or lead dietitian sets the concern and referral rules.

  3. 03 · 2–6 weeksBuild

    We build the workflows in n8n or code, the secure forms and staff dashboards, AI prompts grounded in approved content, and the connections to the client's booking, access and payment systems, all in a staging setup with test data.

  4. 04 · 1–2 weeksValidate & launch

    Staff test real scenarios: a full class with a waitlist, a color client with no patch test on record, a failed UPI Autopay debit, a freeze request outside policy and a check-in that mentions dizziness. We test AI drafts against an evaluation set, launch at one location or with one coaching team first, and train every shift.

  5. 05 · Ongoing, reviewed monthlyOperate & improve

    We monitor workflow health, response times, renewal and no-show measures and AI quality, fix failures, and review results with the owner each month. New locations, services, programs and templates are added through the same approval process.

Suggested first pilot

One location or coaching team, one journey, four to six weeks

We start where leakage is clearest. For a gym or studio that is usually trial booking and follow-up plus attendance-drop alerts at one location. For a salon it is booking, reminders and rebooking at one outlet, and for a coaching business, intake routing and weekly check-ins for one team. A baseline taken in the first week keeps the comparison honest.

  • One location, outlet or coaching team and one member journey
  • Approved WhatsApp templates and secure forms
  • Integration with the gym, salon or coaching software in read and limited write mode
  • A staff dashboard with escalation to a named manager
  • Weekly check-ins and a go or no-go review at the end of the pilot

Measures

Know whether it is working.

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Inquiry first response time

Median time from a new inquiry on WhatsApp, Instagram, Google or a lead form to the first meaningful reply by the system or a person, by channel and hour of day.

Trial-to-member conversion

Trial or intro-offer visitors who buy a membership, class pack or program within an agreed period, divided by trial visitors who attended, by campaign and consultant.

Class and chair utilization

Attended class places, or booked chair, room and therapist hours, as a share of available capacity, by time slot, location and staff member.

No-show and late cancellation rate

Bookings not attended or canceled inside the agreed cutoff, divided by all bookings for the class, service or day.
